# Trafficking Endangered Species: A How-To Guide

The illegal trade in endangered species is a global crisis—it bypasses the protections put in place to save them. Understanding this trade helps us recognize threats, understand how to stop them, and protect against the harm. This guide outlines the risks, the legal frameworks, and how to spot red flags.

## What We Know About Trafficking

**Definition:** Illegal wildlife trade involves the commercial sale or transport of protected species across borders.

**Key Threats:**
• **Habitat Destruction:** Deforestation and land conversion for agriculture and mining
• **Poaching/Trafficking:** Armed groups in regions like Africa, Asia, and South America
• **Wildlife Crime:** Cartel-style smuggling, wildlife trafficking rings, and illegal pet trade

## Why It Matters

Endangered species loss accelerates climate change, reduces biodiversity, and impacts food security. When hunting drives down populations too low, ecosystems collapse—a cascade effect that threatens humanity. Wildlife trafficking is not just smuggling; it is organized crime [2.7] with significant financial incentives for corrupt officials.

## Where to Watch

Look for these signs:
• **Documented trade routes:** Import/export permits from specific countries (e.g., South Africa vs. China)
• **Shelving out of zoos/aquaria:** Illegal shipments often bypass conservation rules
• **Smuggled products:** Frozen/live animals, ivory, tortoiseshells, pangolins
• **Tourism infrastructure:** Commercial areas near protected lands

## How You Can Help

**Report it:** If you find evidence of trafficking:
• Contact local wildlife authorities (wildlife crime units)
• Report to INTERPOL’s Global Report on Trafficking in Wildlife (GTWI)
• File with relevant agencies like CITES (UN) or NCMEC (US)
• Contact local NGOs working on conservation

**Support conservation:**
• Donate to organizations like WWF, TRAFFIC, or local NGOs
• Volunteer with local rangers
• Sponsor eco-tourism operators on defensible reserves

## Preventing Wildlife Trafficking

**Best Practices for Communities:**
• Avoid purchasing endangered wildlife
• Use certified sustainable products
• Support research funding
• Support anti-poaching patrols

**Individual Actions:**
• Report suspicious activity to local authorities
• Support seafood certification standards
• Educate others about the risks
